about.title: About the Data & Methodology
about.subtitle: Water quality criteria, scoring method, and traceability
about.class_b_heading: Why CPCB Class B was chosen
about.class_b_text: Immersion ghats are public water contact sites where citizens and workers enter the water during rituals. Class B ('Outdoor bathing organised') is the closest official CPCB water use classification. Dissolved oxygen must be at least 5 mg/l, BOD no more than 3 mg/l, and pH between 6.5 and 8.5.
about.scoring_heading: Risk scoring method in plain words
about.scoring_step1: 1. Severity calculation: Each tested reading of DO, BOD, and pH is given a severity score from 0 (meets standard) to 1 (severe departure) based on Class B limits.
about.scoring_step2: 2. Weights: DO carries 45% weight, BOD 35%, and pH 20%. Recent years (2025: 1.0, 2024: 0.7, 2023: 0.5) and during/after phases are weighted higher.
about.scoring_step3: 3. Fair handling of missing data: Untested readings (marked 'not sampled') are excluded from both numerator and denominator. Missing data never improves or lowers a score.
about.scoring_step4: 4. Tier threshold: Scores 40 and above (or any critical DO reading ≤ 2 mg/l during recent Durga visarjans) are classified as High risk. Scores 15 to 39 are Medium, and under 15 are Low.
about.limit_do_desc: Dissolved oxygen in water, essential for aquatic balance
about.limit_bod_desc: Biochemical oxygen demand, measures organic matter loading
about.gaps_text: The MPPCB reports do not publish Durga 2025 tables for Bairagarh or Malikhedi. Rani Kamlapati / Kamla Park has slight variations in table naming across festivals. Parameters such as COD, total solids, and turbidity do not have official Class B bathing limits set.
about.sources_text: All data is sourced directly from MPPCB official immersion reports for 2023, 2024, and 2025 without modification.

prioritization.title: Deterministic Risk Scoring Methodology
prioritization.subtitle: How environmental priority tiers are calculated from historical observations
prioritization.step1_desc: Each reading is normalized against CPCB Class B criteria (DO 45% weight, BOD 35%, pH 20%).
prioritization.step2_desc: More recent years (2025: 1.0, 2024: 0.7, 2023: 0.5) and during/after immersion phases receive higher weight.
prioritization.step3_desc: Untested parameters (marked 'not tested') are excluded from numerator and denominator to prevent distorted scores.
prioritization.step4_desc: Score ≥ 40 or critical DO ≤ 2.0 mg/L assigns High Priority; 15–39 assigns Medium Priority; < 15 assigns Low Priority.
